definition: Alzheimer's Disease clinical outcome or disease progression status post-mortem. Used to classify participants into "control", "AD", "Other"
note: Ports the out-of-repo cohort_label_patch.sql AD classification into the committed pipeline: derives the uniform 4234469 AD cohort record FROM ADoutcome. Coexists with mappings/ADoutcome.json (same source column -> 3187945 Neuropathology observable) via the ETL's (variable, defining_concept, source_value) value-map key. AD -> Alzheimer's disease 36311271 (qualifier 1989833 'Admitting diagnosis', case); Control -> Normal 45884153 (qualifier 44804027 'Control group'); Other -> 45878142 'Other' (status). This is what makes AD disease reproducible from `make load` (previously it existed only in the manual patch), restoring S1/S3/S13/S14. FALLBACK: when ADoutcome is the real 'missing or unknown' category (~0.5% of DiverseCohorts, written as blank), the record falls back to mayoDx via COALESCE(NULLIF(ADoutcome,''), NULLIF(mayoDx,'')) -- one value, one record. mayoDx's lowercase 'other'/'not applicable' are mapped for robustness. — Prior definition: AD cohort membership DERIVED from ADoutcome (the post-mortem neuropathological/clinical AD outcome). This is the uniform 4234469 'Diagnosis' cohort record; it does NOT replace ADoutcome's own observation (3187945 Neuropathology observable) -- it derives cohort membership FROM it, alongside it. One per subject; does not change over time. — Extended AMP definition: Derived harmonized outcomes based on CERAD neuritic plaque score and Braak stage, or NINCDS-ADRD criteria for Mayo. The following criteria seek to harmonize outcomes between cohorts as closely as possible, with Mayo’s neuropath-based diagnoses (as determined by Mayo specialists) set as the standard to match. These thresholds will also exclude individuals with age-related tauopathies from being classified as AD cases or controls. sh, MSSM, Columbia derived outcome criteria: AD: Braak ≥ 4, CERAD = Frequent or Moderate Control: Braak ≤ 3, CERAD = Sparse or None Other: all other UFL (from Mayo): some patients from UFL were not consistent with other MayoDx criteria (i.e. 8 individuals had Braak < 4 and a mayoDx==AD). These individuals were assigned ‘Other’ criteria in the ADoutcome variable to harmonize more closely with MayoDx criteria.
